raw_response:
My family farms about 10 mu here in Quzhou. The land is flat, good for the plow, and we've been doing the same rotation since before I was farming on my own — winter wheat in October, harvest in June, then summer maize goes straight in after. Two crops off the same land every year. That's what makes sense here, and that's what everyone around me does.

For wheat, I'll buy improved seed from the county seed station, same as last year. A neighbor tried some new variety from a company rep last season — I'm not interested in that. The improved variety I know gives me 450 jin per mu on a decent year, and that's enough.

Fertilizer: I put down a base application at planting — phosphorus, potassium, some nitrogen — and then I top-dress with urea at jointing. My brother tells me I use too much, but if I cut back and the crop suffers, that's real money gone. I'd rather not find out the hard way.

Water is the expensive part. Wheat needs four irrigations — pre-sowing, winter water, jointing, heading. I can't skip any of those. For maize, the summer rains help, but some years they don't come on time, so I keep two irrigations ready.

Maize I seed directly into the wheat stubble — no-till saves me time and the soil doesn't need to be turned again. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the station has close to it. That's been reliable for years.

Pesticides: one herbicide pass for wheat in spring, one fungicide if I see powdery mildew. For maize, one pass for corn borer in July. I don't spray more than needed because the chemicals cost money and I have to do the work myself.

That's the plan. Same as always, more or less.
